Cancer Dependency Explorer

The question

Which molecular features predict dependency on MDM2 across cancer cell models?

This reproducible target assessment integrates CRISPR dependency with lineage, expression, copy number and damaging somatic mutations from DepMap Public 26Q1. More-negative Chronos scores indicate that knockout has a stronger effect on cell fitness.

6 of 6 checks passed. A failed check is retained in this report rather than silently ignored; critical failures stop the workflow before modelling.

Dependency distribution

Across 1208 models, the median MDM2 Chronos score was -0.426 (interquartile range -0.867 to -0.289). The proportion below -0.5 was 38.4%. These thresholds describe the distribution; they do not establish clinical actionability.

Lineage specificity

The global lineage comparison gave a Kruskal–Wallis P value of 3.8e-25. The lineage with the most-negative median difference from the remaining models was Eye (-1.17 Chronos units). This comparison is descriptive and may reflect molecular differences correlated with lineage.

Target expression and copy number

MDM2 expression showed Spearman rho -0.486 (P = 1.6e-68); MDM2 copy number showed Spearman rho -0.179 (P = 1.2e-07). Correlation does not distinguish a causal biomarker from a feature that tracks cell state or lineage.

Genomic associations

Damaging mutations

The leading mutation association was TP53 (altered-minus-reference effect 0.775, FDR 1.4e-82). A negative effect denotes stronger MDM2 dependency in altered models.

Copy number

The leading copy-number association was RPAP2 (correlation 0.22, FDR 3.6e-07). Correlated loci can represent the same chromosomal event and are filtered for redundancy before multivariable modelling.

Multivariable model

The model used 852 complete models and adjusted for lineage. Its adjusted R² was 0.565; fixed-feature 10-fold cross-validation gave RMSE 0.384 and R² 0.532. Confidence intervals use the HC3 heteroscedasticity-robust estimator.

The strongest adjusted molecular association was TP53 damaging mutation (coefficient 0.511; 95% CI 0.427 to 0.595), corresponding to weaker dependency as the feature increases or is present.

Interpretation and limitations

This analysis nominates molecular correlates of MDM2 dependency; it does not demonstrate causality, druggability or therapeutic efficacy. Results may be influenced by lineage composition, correlated copy-number regions, complete-case selection and unmeasured confounding. Automatic feature discovery and model assessment use the same release, so inferential P values and fixed-feature cross-validation are exploratory rather than independent validation. Cell-line dependencies may not reproduce in tumours or normal tissues, and genetic knockout may not mimic pharmacological inhibition.

The inverse question—which dependencies are selective in models carrying mutation of a chosen tumour suppressor?—requires a different feature-centric genome-wide dependency screen and is intentionally outside this repository’s scope.

Reproducibility

The aggregate outputs, figures and this report can be committed. Raw DepMap matrices and model-level intermediate data remain excluded from Git and must be obtained under their applicable data-use terms.
